surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Bruins shake off a slow start against the Kings
paras: Alex Laferriere struck first for the Kings just 31 seconds into the game, but they didn’t score again. Mark Kastelic and Samuel Helenius fought late in the first. David Pastrňák tied it up for Boston early in the second, and Marat Khusnutdinov put the Bruins ahead 2-1 with less than seven minutes left. Elias Lindholm sealed it into the empty net with just under two minutes left. JJ Peterka added an empty-net goal with 18 seconds left to make it 4-1.

The Kings had a little more of the play, but the Bruins made their chances count. The Bruins had six shots in the first period and trailed 1-0, then outshot the Kings 22-14 the rest of the way. Jeremy Swayman made 25 saves for the Bruins, and Anton Forsberg stopped 24 of 26 at the other end.

Erik Haula picked up a ten-minute misconduct. The Bruins moved to 7-2-0, still first in the Atlantic. The Kings are seventh in the Pacific. The Kings are still looking for their first win of the season, now 0-4-2.
